BandDiagramRequest.title: BandDiagramRequest
BandDiagramRequest.description: What to draw. `parameters` holds every parameter of the mode in core units, as in a curve.

BandDiagramResponse.title: BandDiagramResponse
BandDiagramResponse.description:
Curves over `wavevector_nm_inv` (nm⁻¹), with energies divided by k_B (K).

Null marks a non-finite energy. `reference_mass_assumed` marks DPB diagrams
whose curvature scale assumes a first-band mass magnitude of one electron mass.

CalcRequest.title: CalcRequest
CalcRequest.description:
What to calculate.

`parameters` holds every parameter of the mode in core units, including those of other
scattering types. Values outside a control's range are allowed, as a fit can end there. `points`
defaults to the model's. `measurements` gives an RMSE for each quantity, and should hold only
points in the fit range. `extrapolated` says that interpolation made up some of these points.

`kind` chooses the curves, and `GET /api/models` lists which a mode offers. `measurements` need
the `measured` kind, because the known issues of a response are those of its curves, and an RMSE
of other curves would not carry its own.

core_version.title: Core Version
core_version.description: Core software version for provenance, not certification.

CalcResponse.title: CalcResponse
CalcResponse.description:
Curves by name, where each name ends in its unit, and null marks a value that is not finite.

`known_issues` names known errors that apply to this result, as in `GET /api/models`. `rmse` is
empty without measurements. `measured_points` holds points made from the measurements sent,
by name with its unit: `electrical_conductivity_s_per_m` is 1/rho, with null for a rho of 0 or
below. They use no model, so they go with the data the request sent, interpolated or not.

ColumnRead.title: ColumnRead
ColumnRead.description:
A column as the parser read it. `unit_source` says where its unit came from: `chosen` by the
request, named by the column's `header`, or SI by `default`, as nothing named one. It is left
out where `unit` is, as with errors.

ColumnRole.title: ColumnRole
ColumnRole.description:
What a column holds, and the unit its values are written in. Columns count from 0.

In a request, `unit` is a user's choice, and without it the column's header unit, or SI,
applies. In an answer it is the unit the column was read in. `input-data.md` of the core lists
the units of each quantity.

CurveAvailabilityResponse.title: CurveAvailabilityResponse
CurveAvailabilityResponse.description:
Whether a mode offers a kind of curve for `POST /api/calc`.

`reason` is a code for one it does not offer, and a client shows `curve_unavailable.<reason>`
through i18n. `relative` means that the size of the curve rests on an assumed value, not on
data: carrier concentrations with no Hall data use m1 = 1.

DemoNoise.title: DemoNoise
DemoNoise.description: The noise added to the model's curves: V/K for S, and a relative size for rho and R_H.

DemoResponse.title: DemoResponse
DemoResponse.description:
A parsed file, as from `POST /api/parse`, that is not a measurement of any material.

A client must say so, by showing `message_key` through i18n wherever the data appear.
`known_issues` names the errors of the model that the data carry. `model`, `fit_mode` and
`scattering` say what generated them. `true_parameters` holds values of that model, in core
units, and its other parameters were at the defaults of `GET /api/models`.

EnergyDisplayResponse.title: EnergyDisplayResponse
EnergyDisplayResponse.description:
How a client shows an energy that comes in K, such as a curve of μ or E(k): in `unit`, at
`per_kelvin` of it for each kelvin. Temperatures stay in K.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: One problem in a request. `location` is the path to it, such as `["body", "points", 3]`.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description:
The body of every error response.

`details` holds at most 50 problems, and `details_omitted` counts any more, left out.

FitApiRequest.title: FitApiRequest
FitApiRequest.description:
What to fit.

`start` holds every parameter of the mode in core units, including those of other scattering
types. `bounds` overrides the description's bounds for fitted parameters, in core units.
`measurements` holds each quantity of the mode, and only points from `min_temperature_k` to
`max_temperature_k`, inclusive, enter the fit. `extrapolated` says that interpolation made up
some of these points, so that the result says so too.

`held` names fitted parameters to keep at their start values: the fit finds only the others.
A name the mode does not fit, for the scattering type, or every fitted parameter, is refused.

FitDiagnostics.title: FitDiagnostics
FitDiagnostics.description:
Numerical diagnostics, separate from physical adequacy and uncertainty.

`optimality` is the normalized projected gradient at the returned parameters,
in scaled stage coordinates. Conditional objective-reduction audits also have
to pass before `stage_consistent` can be true.

FitDone.title: FitDone
FitDone.description: The last event of a fit that ended, whatever its `status`.

FitError.title: FitError
FitError.description: The last event of a fit with no result: `fit_timeout`, `fit_process_died` or `fit_failed`.

FitIteration.title: FitIteration
FitIteration.description:
Progress of an iterative fit, in core units. A single-pass mode sends none.

`parameters` holds every parameter of the mode, in the form of a final result. One fitted after
the loop, such as m1, keeps its start value here. A value that is not finite is null.

FitModeResponse.title: FitModeResponse
FitModeResponse.description:
One way of fitting a model.

A client must not offer a mode with `disabled`. `disabled_by` names the `known_issues` that say
why. `iterative` tells whether an iteration count means anything. `threshold`, a relative
change, and `max_iterations` are what an iterative fit uses, and a request cannot change them.
`scattering` is empty when a mode has no choice of scattering. `stages` are the solver runs of
a fit, in their order. `band_2_edge` names the parameter whose core value is the edge of band 2
above that of band 1, in K, and is left out for a mode with one band.

core_version.title: Core Version
core_version.description: Core software version for provenance, not certification.

FitResponse.title: FitResponse
FitResponse.description:
The outcome of a fit, in core units.

`converged` means numerical termination, not physical adequacy or identification.
`stalled` is a usable endpoint that did not converge. `iteration_limit`
is not a converged result. `failed` returns the start values, with fixed text in `message`.
`iterations` is left out for a single-pass mode. A value that is not finite is null.

In the legacy method, `parameter_errors` holds standard errors from the last solver run of
each stage, holding other stages fixed. They can be far too small in a staged fit. The verified
method leaves errors empty and reports uncertainty as `not_assessed`; it does not manufacture
zero errors for profiled or unidentified parameters.
`at_bounds` names fitted parameters that ended at a bound, which may be what set them.
`known_issues` names known errors that apply, as in `GET /api/models`. `held` names the
parameters the request held, which come back as sent, with no error and no at-bound mark; the
errors of the others hold the held values exact. A held value outside its bounds fails as a
start would. Holding m1, or the SPB Hall mass, skips the R_H stage.

`parameter_status` says how the fit found each parameter in `parameters`, the first that
applies of: `held`; `fixed`, not fitted in this mode or scattering; `not_assessed`, a failed
fit or a stage it never reached; `at_bound`; `not_assessed`, a stage with no more points than
parameters, or a legacy error that is not finite; `not_determined`, the data do not depend on
it; `not_assessed`, any other of a fit that did not converge; `did_not_move`, within 1e-9
relative of its start; and `estimated`, which means only that no signal said otherwise. None
says that a value is right. `uncertainty` is `not_assessed` for every fit until confidence
intervals exist (#182).

`last_changes` holds, for an iterative legacy fit, the relative change of each parameter of
its loop in the last iteration, as its stop rule compared it with the mode's `threshold`; the
first iteration compares with the start values, and null is a change that is not finite. The
loop stops by its rule only when every one is at most the threshold. With N2/N1 other than 1,
the first change of m_eff compares with its start divided by N2/N1, so it reads too large
(#85). At `iteration_limit` the loop fits S once more after these changes, so m_eff, E_g and
E_F are from that stage. Otherwise it is empty.

FitStageResponse.title: FitStageResponse
FitStageResponse.description:
One solver run of a fit: the quantity it fits, and the parameters it finds.

`repeats` marks a stage of the loop of an iterative mode, which runs once in each iteration.
`parameters` names every parameter the stage can find; the scattering decides which of them
a fit has.

FitStarted.title: FitStarted
FitStarted.description: The fit has left the queue, and its process is starting.

GuessFound.title: GuessFound
GuessFound.description:
A guess.

`start_values` holds what to use, by the parameter names of `GET /api/models`, in core units as
in `core_range`: `m_eff` is dimensionless, `band_gap` and `fermi_energy` are in K. They are
rounded and limited as the desktop's sliders do, so they lie in `core_range` of every mode of
the model. Other parameters keep their values. With the warning `m_eff_rounds_to_zero`, `m_eff`
is 0, which has no curve, and a fit from it fails, so a client should not use it as it is.

GuessNoNet.title: GuessNoNet
GuessNoNet.description:
No net fits the actual minimum and maximum temperatures.

Legacy first/last fields report the minimum/maximum. Keep the current values.

GuessNotFinite.title: GuessNotFinite
GuessNotFinite.description:
The net ran, but a value of its prediction is not finite, so there is nothing to use.

The prediction is left out, as JSON has no such numbers. A client should keep its values.

GuessRequest.title: GuessRequest
GuessRequest.description:
Measured Seebeck data, in V/K, with all rows of the data.

Unlike `POST /api/calc`, this takes every row and not only the fit range, as the desktop does.
The net is chosen from actual Tmin/Tmax; paired rows are sorted before preparing its input.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: The commit the API was built from, with -dirty for uncommitted changes, or null if unknown. For provenance.

core_version.title: Core Version
core_version.description: Core software version for provenance, not certification.

InterpolatedResponse.title: InterpolatedResponse
InterpolatedResponse.description:
A quantity on the interpolation grid. `null` marks a value that is not finite.

`range_limited` means the requested range extends beyond this quantity's measured range.
`extrapolated` is retained for compatibility and is false for new server results.
`measured_points_in_range` counts source points in the requested range; zero can occur between
sparse measurements. `underdetermined` means that the data do not set the polynomial.

IssueResponse.title: IssueResponse
IssueResponse.description:
A problem in the data, as a code a client translates, in `input-data.md` of the core.

`line` counts every line of the text from 1, and `column` from 0. `direction` says, for
`implausible_magnitude`, whether the largest |value| is `above` the quantity's upper limit or
`below` its lower one. No issue carries a measured value.

KnownIssueResponse.title: KnownIssueResponse
KnownIssueResponse.description:
A known error of the calculations in this mode. Clients show `message_key` through i18n.

Empty `scattering` means every type. `curve_kinds` lists the curves it applies to, and empty
means none. Empty `columns` means every curve of those kinds. `condition`, if present, limits it
to some inputs. `fixed_by` is the issue in this repository that removes it.

MeasuredPointsResponse.title: MeasuredPointsResponse
MeasuredPointsResponse.description: Points made from measurements alone, at their temperatures. Null marks one with no value.

MeasurementInput.title: MeasurementInput
MeasurementInput.description: Measured points, with values in V/K for S, ohm m for rho and m^3/C for R_H.

MeasurementResponse.title: MeasurementResponse
MeasurementResponse.description:
Measured data sorted by temperature, in V/K, ohm m or m^3/C, and its size and range.

`loaded_as` is what the text held: the quantity itself, or `conductivity` for a resistivity
that the core computed as 1/sigma from a column of sigma. Its interpolation, fits and RMSE all
use that resistivity.

ModelResponse.title: ModelResponse
ModelResponse.description:
A model. `name` is English text, for a client to fall back on.

`has_initial_guess` says that `POST /api/guess` gives start values for this model.

NetRange.title: NetRange
NetRange.description: The temperature span a net needs, and the range of its input.

NumericalGuessFound.title: NumericalGuessFound
NumericalGuessFound.description: Seebeck-only estimate; mass magnitude remains a reference value.

ParameterResponse.title: ParameterResponse
ParameterResponse.description:
One parameter of a fit mode.

`display_range` is the control's range as a user sees it, and `core_range` is the same range in
the core units of requests and results. Use these two, and do not calculate core values from the
scales: `display_scale` and `fit_scale`, from control units in `value_range`, are there for
information, as the desktop divides where a multiplication would change the last bit.

In each range, `step` is the desktop's keyboard increment, not a grid: values between steps are
valid, and the default or maximum need not lie on a step.

`scattering` lists the types the parameter applies to, and empty means all of them. A mode with
no choice of scattering uses all its parameters, whatever they list. A `fixed` parameter is set
by the user, and a fit does not change it. Requests hold every parameter of a mode, including
those of other scattering types.

`unit` is the unit of the scaled value, and can be `dimensionless` or `unknown`. `display_unit`
is the one a user sees, and `display_factor` goes from the one to the other: an energy in K is
shown in eV. `display_range` is already in `display_unit`. `fit_bounds` is in core units, and is
left out for a parameter that a fit does not change. `meaning` is English text, for a client
with no translation.

ParseRequest.title: ParseRequest
ParseRequest.description:
A text to read, as the client read it from a file or table.

`expected` names the quantity of a file meant to hold one, and `conductivity` reads its values
as sigma, which comes back as the resistivity 1/sigma. `mapping` replaces the suggested columns
with a user's choice, and the text is sent again each time, as the API keeps nothing.
`interpolate` asks for each quantity on a grid within this range and its measured range.

ParseResponse.title: ParseResponse
ParseResponse.description:
What the text holds. A file with problems is still a 200, with a preview and its `errors`.

`measurements` is empty with any `errors`. `headers` is left out when no header matches the
columns. `column_count` is 0 when neither a row nor a header sets it. `preview` holds the first
rows that could be read, in the order of the text and as read, and `row_count` all of them.
`preview_text` holds the same values exactly as the text writes them, such as `2E+2`, for a
user to compare with the file. `preview_si` holds the same rows in SI, with `null` for a
column with no role or no unit: with `errors`, only a unit the request chose is kept.
`mapping` is the suggestion or the user's choice, and with no readable rows, always the
suggestion. `warnings`
holds every kind, with at most 100 `preamble_skipped`, and `warnings_omitted` counts the rest.
`interpolation_failed` names quantities that could not be interpolated, and
`interpolation_failure_reasons` says why for each: `no_overlap` (the fit range and the measured
range do not overlap), `overlap_too_short` (under 20 K, or under 40 K where the data narrow the
range, which would give one grid point) or `fit_failed` (the polynomial could not be fitted).

Prediction.title: Prediction
Prediction.description: The net's prediction as it is, in core units, before any rounding or limits.

RmseResponse.title: RmseResponse
RmseResponse.description: `value` is null where the result is not finite, as when the model has no finite value.
